identity: Anthropologist and university teacher · United States · 1887–1948
title: Ruth Benedict's birth chart
metaDescription: Ruth Benedict's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 14.7° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Gemini — the Sun, Mercury, Mars and Pluto. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: 14.7° of Gemini is the Sun's exact seat — second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Venus in the old triplicity scheme. The degree is the address; the sign is only the street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Gemini (25.6°), Venus in Cancer (26.5°), Mars in Gemini (4.6°): thought that travels by comparison, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus square Jupiter, 0.0° of separation. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected. Behind it, Mars conjunction Pluto at 0.8°, and Mercury trine Jupiter at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. Mercury in Gemini at 25.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Cancer at 20.7° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 6 air, 2 water, 1 fire, 1 earth by element and 5 mutable, 4 cardinal, 1 fixed by modality. Air signs carry exchange in the scheme — comparison, argument, the sentence that makes the situation legible. Jupiter and Uranus were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.1° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 11.6°.
